citations.long: Written production and process control procedures are not followed in the execution of production and process control functions.
Written procedures for sanitation are not followed.
Records are not kept for the maintenance, cleaning, and inspection of equipment.
Routine calibration of mechanical equipment is not performed according to a written program designed to assure proper performance.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.

citations.short: Testing Each Component for Conformity with Specs
citations.long: Each component is not tested for conformity with all appropriate written specifications for purity, strength, and quality.
Procedures designed to prevent objectionable microorganisms in drug products not required to be sterile are not established.
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed and documented at the time of performance.
Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.

citations.short: Changes to Procedures Not Reviewed, Approved
citations.long: Changes to written procedures are not reviewed and approved by the quality control unit.
Written procedures are not established that describe the in-process controls and tests to be conducted on appropriate samples of in-process materials of each batch.
Deviations from production time limits are not justified.

Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.

citations.short: Drug products - samples representative, identified properly
citations.long: Samples taken of drug products for determination of conformance to written specifications are not representative and properly identified.

citations.short: Labeling control records including specimens or copies
citations.long: Batch production and control records do not include complete labeling control records, including specimens or copies of all labeling used for each batch of drug product produced.
Written production and process control procedures are not followed in the execution of production and process control functions.
Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.
Routine calibration of mechanical equipment is not performed according to a written program designed to assure proper performance.

Written procedures are lacking which describe in sufficient detail the receipt, identification, storage, handling, sampling, testing, approval, and rejection of components, drug product containers, and closures.

citations.short: Testing Each Component for Conformity with Specs
citations.long: Each component is not tested for conformity with all appropriate written specifications for purity, strength, and quality.

citations.short: Control procedures to monitor and validate performance
citations.long: Control procedures are not established which monitor the output and validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
Drug product expiration dates are not related to the storage conditions stated on the labeling, as determined by stability studies.

Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.

Testing and release of drug product for distribution do not include appropriate laboratory determination of satisfactory conformance to the final specifications and identity and strength of each active ingredient prior to release.
There is no written testing program designed to assess the stability characteristics of drug products.
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications.
Written records of investigations into the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and follow-up.

citations.short: Complete test data included in records
citations.long: Laboratory records do not include complete data derived from all tests, examinations and assay necessary to assure compliance with established specifications and standards.

Laboratory records do not include the initials or signature of a second person showing that the original records have been reviewed for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established standards.
